1990-03: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church complained against New River Presbytery's action sustaining a complaint that a Sunday school teacher holding theistic evolution and other doctrinal exceptions should not teach. The SJC partially sustained the complaint, declining to refer the matter back to the church with instructions but advising that the teacher should not teach while he holds exceptions that could require him to teach contrary to the fundamentals of the system of doctrine.
1990-04: Ruling Elder Chappell complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's Commission, which had suspended the session of Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church and constituted itself as a 'Session Pro Tem' without due process or congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO grants no authority for a presbytery to depose a session and act in its place, that suspension requires due process, and that the congregation has an inalienable right to be governed by officers it has chosen.
1990-04a: Teaching Elder Wallace Marshall complained against the same Eastern Carolina Presbytery actions at Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church that were the subject of Case 90-4, filed separately as a Teaching Elder complainant. The SJC sustained this complaint on essentially the same grounds as Case 90-4, finding that the presbytery lacked authority to suspend the session without due process and to constitute itself as a 'Session Pro Tem.'
1990-05: Complainants challenged the ruling of the session of Westminster Presbyterian Church (Chattanooga) disallowing proxy votes at a December 10, 1989 congregational meeting that voted not to rescind the earlier dissolution and property transfer to New City Fellowship. The SJC denied all specifications, holding that proxy voting was not required under BCO 24-4 or Robert's Rules, and that the congregation's decision to dissolve was within its rights under BCO Chapter 25.
1990-07: Randy Stringer appealed his excommunication by Mississippi Valley Presbytery after being deposed and then excommunicated for failure to respond to the presbytery. The SJC set aside the excommunication and remanded the case to MVP, holding that after deposition the presbytery was required under BCO 46-8 to assign Stringer to membership in a particular church rather than proceed to excommunication. Dr. Morton H. Smith dissented, arguing that the presbytery had proper grounds to proceed to excommunication after Stringer's contumacy.
1990-08: TE David Bowen complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's actions rescinding its 1988 decision and annulling the elections and ordinations of ruling elders and deacons at the Church of the Good Shepherd who took exception to infant baptism and limited atonement. The SJC sustained the complaint that ECP erred in rescinding a two-year-old action and annulling ordinations without due process under BCO 24-6, while also affirming that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals of the system of doctrine for which no exceptions may be granted for church officers.
1990-09: TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church failed to institute discipline against seven members who had not attended worship for over a year. The judicial panel denied the complaint on the grounds that the Session retained discretion to determine the timing of discipline proceedings, and procedural errors did not result in material prejudice.
1990-10: TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church refused to furnish him, as pastor and member of the Session, with copies of financial reports the Session had authorized. The panel found Specification 6 sustained (the pastor had a right to the reports as a session member) but declared the complaint moot because Hathaway's pastoral relation had been terminated before the case was decided.
1991-02: Bruce Nickoley and David Stephens complained against Southwest Presbytery's actions in withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving a pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of a local church session. The SJC denied the complaint, affirming that the Presbytery correctly determined it lacked constitutional authority to suspend the session or act as a 'Session pro tem' without congregational consent, and that original jurisdiction over charges against ruling elders rested with the local session.
1991-06: Mrs. Sandra Lovelace complained against Northeast Presbytery's decision not to proceed to trial against teaching and ruling elders, and its ruling that her subsequent complaints were out of order due to non-membership. The SJC (reversing the Judicial Panel) denied the first item but sustained the second, holding that jurisdiction properly invoked is not forfeited by a subsequent change in the complainant's membership status.
1992-01: Frank J. Smith complained against Northeast Presbytery after Grace Presbyterian Church was dissolved and its members were placed under Presbytery's care. The SJC ruled the complaint in order, sustained it, and returned the matter to Presbytery for adjudication, holding that dissolution did not eliminate Presbytery's pastoral responsibility or Smith's standing in the pending case.
1992-02: Virgil B. Roberts complained that New River Presbytery delayed dissolving his pastoral relationship after he resigned and the congregation concurred. The SJC sustained the complaint, concluding that Presbytery should have acted on the agreed request rather than withholding dissolution; three commissioners dissented concerning Presbytery's constitutional authority and pastoral discretion.
1992-03: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.
1992-04: Robert D. Hopper, pastor of Grace Covenant Church in Williamsburg, Virginia, challenged James River Presbytery's April 1991 action forbidding him from preaching and teaching views affirming that the extraordinary gifts of the Holy Spirit (including prophecy and tongues) may be present in the church in the present age. The Standing Judicial Commission denied the complaint, holding that presbytery has constitutional authority under BCO 13-9 and 34-5 to restrict teaching and preaching when it determines such views may be harmful to the spiritual welfare of the churches under its care, and that such restriction does not violate liberty of conscience absent a determination that the forbidden teaching is heretical.
1992-06: Central Carolina Presbytery remanded complaints to an Interim Session Commission rather than adjudicating them directly. The SJC confirmed this action, finding that the Commission appointed as Interim Session was the proper court of original jurisdiction and remanding the complaints for adjudication by that Commission.
1992-08: The Standing Judicial Commission declined to adjudicate a reference from Central Carolina Presbytery regarding complaints by William A. Conrad against the Interim Session of Prosperity Presbyterian Church. The panel found that additional related complaints had been lodged that were not formally referred to the Commission, and adjudicating the referred matters would render these additional complaints moot without giving them proper consideration under BCO 41-5. The case was referred back to the Central Carolina Presbytery.
1992-09a: Antioch Session complained that Eastern Carolina Presbytery erred in licensing Arthur Peterson given his divorce/remarriage history and his views on creation and a local flood. The SJC did not sustain the complaint on Issue 1 (licensure approval, 13-4), finding ECP acted with constitutional thoroughness and that precedent permitted a divorced man to hold office under certain conditions, but did sustain Issue 2 (3-0 panel; 17-0 SJC), finding ECP negligent in allowing Peterson to serve as stated supply for over six months before licensing him.
1992-09b: Robert J. Overman, III complained against the Eastern Carolina Presbytery's licensing of Arthur Peterson. The Standing Judicial Commission found the complaint not in order due to lack of standing, as the complainant is not subject to the jurisdiction of the Eastern Carolina Presbytery (BCO 43-1; MSJC 6.2). Approved unanimously by the full Commission.
1992-10: Appeal by Mr. and Mrs. Matthew Bernard against an excommunication censure imposed by the Session of Church of the Savior, Williamsville, New York (a Commission of Presbytery appointed by Ascension Presbytery). The Standing Judicial Commission determined the appeal was administratively out of order because it had not been heard by the next higher court (Ascension Presbytery) before being brought to the General Assembly. The Commission held that appeals must go to the next higher court, not the court of original jurisdiction.
1993-01: Frank J. Smith challenged Northeast Presbytery's actions surrounding the dissolution of Grace Presbyterian Church and the administration of its former members. The SJC denied the complaint by a 20-2 vote, with a dissent disputing the majority's treatment of the complainant's constitutional and procedural claims.
1993-02: Edgar Davis Johnson appealed Evangel Presbytery's judgment in a disciplinary case arising from his pursuit of divorce on a claim of spiritual desertion. The SJC did not sustain the appeal, approving the proposed decision by a 21-1 vote.
1993-05: John P. Clark, Jr. requested clarification of the SJC decision in Case 93-5 regarding who controls the assets of South Valley Presbyterian Church, Inc. after the congregation voted to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC held it lacked jurisdiction over the civil corporate entity and its property, declining to rule on Clark's request.
1993-10: TE John P. Clark, Jr. appealed his conviction for contumacy and suspension/deposition by Southwest Presbytery's Judicial Commission. The SJC found the appeal in order (17-4) and remanded the case for retrial (21-0) on grounds that the Judicial Commission committed significant procedural errors, including abandoning original charges and convicting Clark of contumacy on new charges without giving him opportunity to respond.
1993-10b: Case 93-10B arose from Southwest Presbytery's action at its June 14, 1994 meeting declaring TE Clark's suspension 'still binding' notwithstanding his appeal. The SJC held the issue moot in light of its judgment in Case 93-10 remanding the entire matter to the Presbytery for retrial.
1993-11: Paul McDade complained that Susquehanna Valley Presbytery erred in investigating rather than immediately trying charges against session members and pastors for allegedly upholding a false doctrine of repentance and forgiveness. The SJC denied all five specifications, finding the Presbytery followed proper procedure and that no doctrinal error or slander was established.
1993-12: TE Steve Newton appealed his conviction for contumacy and indefinite suspension from office by Heartland Presbytery's judicial commission for persistent failure to submit statistical reports and refusal to cooperate with Presbytery committees. The SJC affirmed Heartland Presbytery's judgment in all respects, with a concurring opinion finding three of four specifications invalid but deferring to the lower court's factfinding on the remaining specification.
1995-10: TE Stuart Merriam, a minister transferred from PCUSA to Tennessee Valley Presbytery in 1986, was subject to ecclesiastical discipline based on his criminal conviction in Papua New Guinea. The SJC sustained Merriam's appeal, finding that TVP violated due process principles and procedures under the BCO, particularly by failing to appoint counsel and conducting an inadequate trial. The case was remanded to TVP for a new trial following proper BCO procedures.
1995-11: Complainants challenged Mississippi Valley Presbytery's approval of James Blaha's theological examination for ordination regarding his views on charismatic gifts. The Special Judicial Commission upheld the challenge regarding prophecy (finding Blaha's views allow possibility of continuing revelation contrary to WCF 1.1 and 6), but rejected the challenge regarding tongues (finding private prayer language use within bounds of 1974 Pastoral Letter). Commission ordered presbytery to note prophecy exception in minutes and instruct Blaha not to teach or preach this view.
1996-06: The panel action on Case 96-6 was approved, dismissing the complaint on the grounds that it was judicially out of order because the parties could not agree on the Record of the Case.
1997-02: Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in immediately deposing Rev. Bruce Nickoley for contumacy without giving him reasonable opportunity to defend himself under the due process provisions of the Book of Church Order. The case was remanded to the presbytery with recommendations to either institute a formal prosecution with due process or revoke the deposition and reinstate Nickoley.
1997-03: The SJC found that Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in immediately deposing Rev. Bruce Nickoley from ministry on a contumacy charge without providing him due process rights and a full trial. The case was remanded for either proper trial or revocation of the deposition judgment.
1997-04: Central Carolina Presbytery did not act unconstitutionally in denying the complaint of Conrad, et al. against the Session of Prosperity Presbyterian Church. Although various actions taken by the parties were open to differing opinions and interpretations, the complainants failed to demonstrate any unconstitutional procedure or violations of the PCA Book of Church Order.
1997-05: The Mt. Carmel Session complained that New Jersey Presbytery erred by adopting a resolution of Affirmations and Denials Regarding the Interpretation of Genesis One that denied the 24-hour-day view as the only acceptable interpretation. The SJC majority denied the complaint (12-9), holding that NJP acted within its constitutional authority under BCO 11-4 to resolve questions of doctrine, consistent with prior General Assembly decisions allowing latitude on creation-day interpretation; a minority report was filed and the case was referred to the 26th General Assembly for final disposition.
1997-06: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained an appeal by E. L. Fitzsimmons against Evangel Presbytery's handling of his appeal from excommunication. The court found that Presbytery erred by failing to notify the appellant of the time, date, and place for hearing the appeal and by rescinding its earlier finding that the appeal was in order, thus failing to adjudicate the appeal properly. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper adjudication on the merits.
1997-07: TE Jeffrey Black's complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's July 1999 ruling that a transferring licentiate's view on the length of the creation days did not constitute an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC Panel affirmed the presbytery's decision, finding no error in the presbytery's handling of the matter.
1997-08: The Standing Judicial Commission found the complaint judicially out of order because the complainant was not a member of a PCA church and therefore lacked standing before the Commission.
1997-10: Case 97-10 - Raymond Larsen vs. Pacific Presbytery (Complaint) was withdrawn by the complainant. No full decision text found; case appears only as a docket list entry on p. 105 with the notation that it was withdrawn by complainant.
1997-11: Appeal of Raymond Larsen v. Pacific Presbytery challenging his deposition from Calvary Presbyterian Church Session. Appeal found to be administratively out of order because only those who have submitted to regular trial are entitled to appeal under BCO 42-2, and Larsen was deposed for contumacy regarding failure to appear for trial.
1997-12: Case was withdrawn by complainant before decision. Listed in the docket of cases before the Standing Judicial Commission at the 26th General Assembly (1998).
1997-13: The SJC sustained the complaint of the Session of Harvestwood Presbyterian Church against New River Presbytery, holding that Presbytery erred in ruling on the acceptability of a Sunday school teacher without having the matter properly referred for final disposition or through appeal/complaint channels, and without an adequate record of what the teacher actually believed regarding theological matters such as theistic evolution and the historicity of Adam.
1997-15: Case was deemed abandoned due to death of Complainant without heirs. The case appears only as a docket notation in the judicial commission proceedings.
1997-16: Complaint against Central Carolina Presbytery was not sustained by a vote of 11-7. Two dissenting opinions were recorded.
1997-17: Dennis Lebo complained that Susquehanna Valley Presbytery erred in denying his complaint that the congregation of Carlisle Reformed Presbyterian Church acted unconstitutionally when it voted to supplement the Assistant Pastor's Fund. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the congregation's action did not violate BCO 12-5b because the Session retained authority to approve and adopt the final budget.
1998-01: Byron Snapp complained that James River Presbytery erred in sustaining the ordination examination of a candidate who held an 'anthropomorphic' view of creation days rather than literal 24-hour days. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Presbytery acted within its constitutional authority to sustain the examination and that the 26th GA had not yet resolved the constitutional status of such views.
1998-02: St. Paul Session and others complained that Central Florida Presbytery erred in sustaining the report of a commission that investigated but did not bring to trial charges against TE John Hutchinson, and also regarding a related complaint against the Session of Christ Church, Jacksonville. The SJC denied the complaint, finding CFP acted within its right to determine investigation procedures under BCO 31-2, with a dissent arguing CFP failed to investigate the substance of the 45 specific charges.
1998-03: The panel action on Case 98-3 was approved, dismissing the appeal on the grounds that it was administratively out of order.
1998-05: Harry Long and others complained that James River Presbytery erred by instructing ordained TE Andrew Conrad not to teach or preach his views on creation days after granting him an exception. The SJC denied the complaint, deferring to the Presbytery's discretion, with a dissent arguing that the liberty of conscience principles and prior GA decisions made the instruction to Conrad inappropriate.
1998-06: Case 98-6 was declared no longer in order because the complainant and others had withdrawn from the PCA to form an independent congregation, and BCO 43-1 requires a complainant to be a communing member of the church subject to the court's jurisdiction.
1998-07: Case 98-7 was declared administratively out of order on the grounds that the complainant did not file a complaint after the Presbytery dealt with the case in a called meeting.
1998-08: Beverly R. Smith appealed her conviction on four charges (factiousness, gossip/slander, breaking membership vows, and contumacy) by the session of Covenant Presbyterian Church, which was upheld by Southwest Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, finding the documentary evidence insufficient to prove the charges and that the session committed multiple procedural errors including failure to produce witnesses, prejudice, and improper suspension from the sacraments before charges were disclosed.
1998-09: Teaching Elder David Baer appealed his suspension by Illiana Presbytery after being found guilty of violating the 9th commandment and ordination/installation vows by falsely telling his congregation that the session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks. The SJC denied the appeal, affirming the presbytery's finding of guilt and the censure of indefinite suspension pending repentance.
1998-10: Eastern Carolina Presbytery referred TE Byron Curtis's complaint to the SJC after ECP had prohibited him from teaching his exceptions to the Westminster Standards (including an exception on six-day creation). The SJC panel returned the matter to ECP with instructions that Curtis's complaint be heard by the lower court, finding it was premature for the SJC to adjudicate while the lower court had not yet considered the substance of the complaint.
1999-01: Western Carolina Presbytery and two other presbyteries requested the General Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over a teaching elder regarding allegations that women preachers filled the pulpit at Cedar Springs Presbyterian Church. The Standing Judicial Commission dismissed the matter as not properly before the General Assembly, ruling that the conduct of worship services is under the jurisdiction of the Session, not subject to process against a minister under BCO 34-1, and that Tennessee Valley Presbytery did act on the allegations.
1999-02: TE Aureliano Tan's complaint against South Texas Presbytery was declared administratively out of order as not timely filed, because the complaint was dated and faxed on August 28 but not mailed until September 4, 1999, exceeding the 30-day filing period specified in BCO 43-3 and the SJC Manual.
1999-04: The Standing Judicial Commission found that Evangel Presbytery erred in failing to notify appellant E.L. Fitzsimmons of the time and place of the hearing on his appeal and in failing to adjudicate the appeal once it was found to be in order. The case was remanded to Evangel Presbytery for proper rehearing and adjudication in accordance with BCO 42-8.
1999-05: Covenant Presbytery properly divested Teaching Elder Lawrence Rountree without censure after he remained on presbytery rolls for over seven years without a valid call to ministry, residing outside presbytery bounds, with no prospects for ministry. The Standing Judicial Commission sustained presbytery's divestiture action as constitutional and appropriate.
1999-06: The SJC reversed the session's imposition of excommunication on Dr. Robert Shive for inappropriate conduct while counseling female patients, remanding instead for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, finding insufficient evidence of contumacy or impenitence to justify the highest censure.
2000-02: TE Philip J. Adams complained about a Northeast Presbytery judicial matter while a related appeal was pending and sought a retrial of charges on which the accused had been acquitted. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-1 and because the requested relief was unavailable. A separate opinion concurred in the result but dissented from part of the reasoning and urged clarification of appellate review after an acquittal.
2000-03: Memorial from South Coast Presbytery that was withdrawn before the Standing Judicial Commission rendered a decision on the merits.
2000-04: The SJC found the complaint filed by Thomas Clark Staley against North Texas Presbytery to be out of order on the grounds that Mr. Staley had no standing as he was not a member of a PCA church. The decision turned on the jurisdictional requirement that only PCA church members may bring complaints before the Standing Judicial Commission.
2000-05: Complaint filed by Robert H. King against Evangel Presbytery. Case was abandoned by complainant and appears in docket as mention only.
2000-08: Complaint of Session of Korean Presbyterian Church of Washington vs. Korean Capital Presbytery was found to be prematurely filed because the Presbytery had not completed its action on the complaint. The Standing Judicial Commission dismissed the case as not yet ripe for judicial review.
2000-10: Case dismissed as out of order because the complaint was not timely filed within 30 days following the meeting of the lower court as required by BCO 43-3.
2001-02: Appeal of suspension from ministry. TE Sang Soo Ryoo appealed his suspension imposed by Korean Capital Presbytery's commission on charges of heresy and schism. The SJC found that Presbyterian judicial procedures were not followed as required by BCO 32, particularly regarding proper service of indictment and notice. The case was therefore remanded to Presbytery for a new trial in compliance with BCO 32.
2001-06: The Korean Eastern Presbytery's Administrative Commission exceeded its authority under BCO 13-9 by calling and facilitating a congregational meeting to vote on ruling elders without proper BCO authority, as complaint procedures under BCO 25-2 and 43 should have been followed instead. The SJC sustained the complaint, reaffirming precedents limiting presbytery power and the principle that a higher court may not 'act for' a lower court.
2001-11: Complaint of RE Byung Han Yoo against Korean Northwest Presbytery was found out of order because it was not timely filed under BCO 43-2, with the action complained of occurring on October 10, 2000 but the complaint filed on March 12, 2001, well outside the 30-day filing period.
2001-13: The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the Korean Capital Presbytery's censure of Deacon Samuel Hong, finding that the Presbytery lacked original jurisdiction over communicant members and should have been tried in the Session. The court held that regardless of the merits of the underlying charges (contumacy and making false statements), the procedural violation of jurisdiction was fatal to the action.
2001-15: In an appeal of an excommunication, the Standing Judicial Commission held that the Session of the local church, not the Presbytery, has original jurisdiction over charges against a communicant member. The court reversed the Special Judicial Commission's action for assuming jurisdiction contrary to constitutional standards.
2001-16: Appeal by RE Joo Bok Suh challenging the Korean Capital Presbytery's attempt to exercise original jurisdiction over charges of making false statements on official documents related to church trustee replacement. The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the presbytery's action, holding that original jurisdiction over communicant members must reside with the Session of the church to which they belong, not with the Presbytery.
2001-17: The Standing Judicial Commission reversed the Korean Capital Presbytery's action in adjudicating charges against RE Choon Soon Lee. The court held that a ruling elder member of a local congregation may only be subject to judicial process originating in the Session of that church, not in the Presbytery, as the Session has original jurisdiction over its members.
2001-18: The Standing Judicial Commission found that the Judicial Commission of Korean Capital Presbytery did not follow proper procedures under BCO 32 and 34 in adjudicating charges against appellant TE Sang Soo Ryoo. Specifically, no indictment was ever properly served on the accused, and there was no clear record of proceedings. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with full compliance to BCO 32 and 34 procedures.
2001-24: Complaint of RE Keith A. Williams vs. Eastern Carolina Presbytery, docketed in 2001 but withdrawn prior to Standing Judicial Commission hearing. Case was listed in the docket at the 30th General Assembly (2002) but withdrew before decision could be rendered.
2001-25: TE Anthony Dallison appealed his deposition from the office of Teaching Elder by North Florida Presbytery, arguing that presbytery lacked authority to increase his censure from indefinite suspension to deposition without conducting a new trial. The SJC affirmed presbytery's decision, holding that where a teaching elder has confessed guilt under BCO 38-1, presbytery may impose additional censure based on evidence of impenitence without initiating new charges, and such disciplinary discretion is within presbytery's constitutional authority.
2001-28: TE Larry Ball complained that Westminster Presbytery erred in approving a plan to withdraw from the PCA. The SJC affirmed that a presbytery has the constitutional right to withdraw from the PCA as part of historic American grass-roots Presbyterianism, subject to proper procedures. The court held that the relationship between General Assembly and presbytery mirrors that between presbytery and local church, protecting each level's distinct identity and civil operations.
2001-30: The SJC ruled the complaint was not judicially in order because PCA church courts lack jurisdiction to serve as civil arbitrators or to conduct appellate review of legally binding arbitration judgments, even if both parties are under PCA jurisdiction. The case arose from a church-school lease and financial dispute resolved through Presbytery-administered binding arbitration.
2001-31: In light of the SJC's decision in Case 2001-33, the April 21, 2001 ECP judgment reversing Jeansonne's conviction stands, and the case was remanded to the Session of Christ Presbyterian Church. BCO 43-1 prohibits complaints in judicial cases where an appeal has been taken.
2001-32: The SJC ruled the case was not judicially in order because the Session of Christ Covenant Church should not have received the original complaint, which was filed more than 30 days after the verdict was received, exceeding the time limit under BCO 43-2. The underlying dispute concerned a session trial commission's acquittal of a member charged with abandonment and seeking an unbiblical divorce.
2001-33: The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that ECP erred in hearing and acting on RE Williams' complaint on July 21, 2001 because BCO 43-1 prohibits complaints in judicial cases where an appeal has been taken. The word 'taken' refers to any appeal whether past, current, or pending, and ECP's action rescinding its prior judgment was therefore improper.
2001-34: Case 2001-34 was decided with Cases 2002-02 and 2002-03. The SJC ruled one constituent complaint out of order, sustained the central challenge to James River Presbytery's delay in acting on a proper congregational request to dissolve a pastoral relationship, and denied the challenge to Presbytery's salary gift. The consolidated decision drew concurring and dissenting opinions.
2001-36: Case was ruled moot due to decisions in related cases 2000-9 and 2001-8 involving Korean Capital Presbytery. No opinion or findings rendered.
2002-01: The SJC affirmed KEP's denial of the appeal regarding the underlying guilty verdicts, but sustained the error of increasing the censure from suspension to excommunication and deposition on appeal, holding that appellate courts may not increase censures beyond what the trial court imposed. The case arose from discipline of two ruling elders who refused to recognize the results of a congregational election.
2002-04: Evangel Presbytery referred a matter to the Standing Judicial Commission for adjudication (Case 2002-04). The SJC did not accede to the request to accept and act upon the judicial reference.
2002-05: Mrs. Plowman was suspended from the Lord's Table and found guilty of contumacy by the Session of Lehigh Valley Presbyterian Church after refusing to compel her minor daughters to testify; her subsequent appeal was informally rejected by the chairman of Presbytery's Judicial Business Committee, who advised her to refile as a complaint. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that Mrs. Plowman had submitted to regular trial and had a right to appeal, and remanded the case to Philadelphia Presbytery for adjudication.
2002-09: TE Merriam appealed his conviction by Tennessee Valley Presbytery on charges of violating ordination vows, including being contumacious toward brethren, failing to maintain church peace, and lacking exemplary piety. The SJC denied the appeal, finding no clear error by the lower court and affirming TVP's procedures and judgment.
2002-10: The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that the Session of Faith Presbyterian Church failed to follow BCO 38-4 procedures when it attempted to retroactively erase Carolyn Goerig's membership after banning her from attending services, and that the Presbytery erred in denying her complaint. Because her membership transfer to another church was never completed, she remained under Faith PC's jurisdiction per BCO 46-3.
2002-11: The SJC largely denied TE Abshire's complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, finding that the Presbytery did not err in appointing a judicial commission or issuing a pastoral exhortation, but sustained the error in the commission's ruling on Lynch and Rooney's complaint without following BCO 43 procedures, remanding that specific matter to Presbytery.
2002-13: The Standing Judicial Commission held that Philadelphia Presbytery did not act unconstitutionally in appointing a commission to hear a memorial from RE David Lachman and adopting its report. The Commission found no evidence of gross unconstitutional proceedings by the Presbytery or its subordinate commission, and upheld the Presbytery's procedures for handling memorials under BCO 40-5.
2002-14: RE Lachman appealed his conviction by the Session of Calvary Presbyterian Church on charges of violating the fifth, sixth, and ninth commandments through contentious correspondence and conduct, arguing the prosecution relied solely on documentary evidence without calling witnesses. The SJC denied the appeal, holding that documentary evidence combined with the appellant's acknowledgment of the letters constituted sufficient witness testimony; a concurring opinion recommended that Sessions facing strained relations with an accused elder consider referring such cases to Presbytery.
2002-15: Complaint of TE Walter Bjorck against Northern New England Presbytery; found administratively out of order by the SJC (31st GA, 2003).
2002-16: The Session of Delhi Presbyterian Church complained that Louisiana Presbytery improperly assumed original jurisdiction over church member Mike Holland, barring him from the Lord's Table for contumacy after he was cited in SPLC reporting regarding Auburn Avenue Presbyterian Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that because Delhi Session had investigated and acted under BCO 31-2, Louisiana Presbytery lacked grounds to assume original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, rendering its judgment against Holland a nullity; three dissenting opinions argued the SJC lacked appellate review of the jurisdiction question because no timely complaint was filed against the assumption of jurisdiction itself.
2003-02: Westminster Presbytery erred in not conducting a complete BCO 31-2 investigation into the secret taping of a phone conversation by TE Frank Smith; the matter was remanded for proper investigation with witness testimony and examination of legal consequences. The complaint regarding partiality and unbiblical criteria for discipline was not proven by complainant.
2003-03: Appeal by TE Paul W. Lee against Korean Southwest Presbytery's judgment finding him guilty of disobeying citations, rejecting admonitions, and other charges. The Standing Judicial Commission found KSWP erred on all issues through procedural violations including improper admonishment of judicial commission members mid-trial, failure to record trial proceedings, denial of cross-examination rights, and improper censure. Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.
2003-06: RE Paul M. Wright filed a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery regarding its response to a Reference from White Oak Presbyterian Church Session on a doctrinal issue. The SJC found the case judicially out of order because the Presbytery's action was advice only in response to a Reference for advice under BCO 41-1, and such advisory actions are not complainable under BCO 43. The Panel recommended the case be found out of order. Vote: 17 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE J. Howard Donahoe), 1 abstaining, 4 absent.
2004-04: The Standing Judicial Commission found the appeal of TE John P. Jerguson against Western Carolina Presbytery to be judicially out of order under BCO 42-2 because the case was not ready for higher court review as it was being reheard by the Presbytery. The case was unanimously concurred upon by 20 commissioners with no dissents.
2004-05: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled that the Blevins/Seufert complaint filed in June 2003 against Westminster Presbytery's Session was timely, holding that when new testimony surfaces (Presbytery's February 2003 ruling recognizing adultery as biblical grounds for divorce), a new 30-day window opens for filing complaints about the court's new judgment on that evidence. Westminster Presbytery erred in dismissing the complaint as untimely.
2004-07: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of the Session of First Presbyterian Church, Augusta, finding that Savannah River Presbytery erred in annulling the Session's actions to dissolve the official relationship with eleven ruling elders. The SJC held that BCO 25-2 does not prohibit a Session from adding agenda items to congregational meetings called pursuant to petitions, and that BCO 24-6 does not prevent a Session from informing the congregation of this right and recommending its exercise.
2004-08: TE James Thornton complained that Westminster Presbytery erred by declining to place a valid call from Memorial PCA into his hands and simultaneously invoking BCO 34-10 to begin divestiture proceedings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the administrative remedy of BCO 34-10 cannot be invoked when a call is already in the presbytery's possession, and that presbytery's refusal lacked objective, justifiable grounds required for appellate review.
2004-09: RE Scott Robar appealed his conviction by Central Carolina Presbytery but filed notice of appeal only with the presbytery's stated clerk, not with the General Assembly's stated clerk as required by BCO 42-4. The SJC found the appeal judicially out of order due to improper filing. A dissenting opinion argued for equitable treatment where the presbytery's own stated clerk had given Robar incorrect advice, citing the Plowman precedent.
2004-12: Case of complaint by ME Hunt vs. Western Carolina Presbytery. The case appeared on the SJC docket for 2004 but was found out of order and therefore not decided on the merits.
2005-01: TE Michael Chastain appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Heritage Presbytery for divisive behavior, arising from his public letters to his congregation disagreeing with Session actions regarding an associate pastor call and a related Christian school controversy. The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.
2005-03: Case listed in the SJC docket as 'Complaint of Session of Living Word PC vs. Pacific NW Presbytery' but was found out of order and not heard on the merits. Living Word Church withdrew from the denomination on 11/16/05.
2005-04: Complaint of Session of Hudson Korean American PC vs. Korean Eastern Presbytery was found out of order by the Standing Judicial Commission at the 34th General Assembly (2006) and therefore no decision on the merits was issued.
2005-05: Wichter Memorial regarding case 2004-05 (Blevins v. Westminster Presbytery). Case found in order but not heard by the Standing Judicial Commission.
2005-06: Case found out of order and not heard on the merits. The complaint of RE Hugo Andrino against Southern Florida Presbytery was procedurally deficient.
2005-08: TE Peter B. Kim appealed his deposition and excommunication by Korean Eastern Presbytery on charges of contumacy and threatening members with civil litigation. The SJC sustained the contumacy charge and deposition but reduced the excommunication to indefinite suspension from the sacraments as excessive; it declined to rule on the civil-threat charge because the relevant letter was not in the Record of the Case.
2005-09: TE Peter B. Kim complained that Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in denying his complaint regarding unconstitutional actions of KEP's Administrative Commission, which had unlawfully exercised judicial powers in ordering a congregational meeting and dissolving his pastoral relationship. The SJC agreed KEP erred but held the matter moot in light of Kim's deposition in Case 2005-8, with a dissent arguing the constitutional violations by KEP were serious and should have been remedied.
2005-10: Memorial of Southern Florida Presbytery was found out of order by the Standing Judicial Commission at the 34th General Assembly (2006) and therefore no decision on the merits was issued.
2005-12: Case 2005-12 was a complaint filed by TE Peter B. Kim against Korean Eastern Presbytery. The case was found to be out of order and was not heard on its merits by the Standing Judicial Commission.
2006-02: Central Carolina Presbytery sent a memorial alleging that TE J. Steven Wilkins of Louisiana Presbytery was teaching doctrines (Federal Vision/Auburn Avenue theology) in flagrant contradiction to the Westminster Standards regarding election, covenant, and baptism. The SJC, after extended proceedings and directing Louisiana Presbytery to re-examine TE Wilkins, found Louisiana Presbytery had not adequately addressed the concerns and directed it via amends to appear under BCO 40-5 to account for its actions.
2006-03: Request for Original Jurisdiction filed by Calvary Presbytery regarding S. Wilkins. The SJC found the case to be out of order, meaning it was not properly before the court and thus was not heard.
2006-04: Case was found out of order and not heard on the merits. No decision rendered.
2006-06: Complaint of Devin and Tracey Ehrlich against North Georgia Presbytery regarding the Presbytery's denial of the Ehrlichs' complaint about the Intown Community Church Session's instruction prohibiting distribution of an open letter criticizing a pastor under investigation. The SJC held that the Session acted within its authority in preventing distribution of the letter, as it would disturb the peace of the church after the Presbytery had investigated and dismissed the underlying allegations against the pastor.
2006-07: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.
2007-03: Case dismissed as procedurally out of order. Listed in GA 36 (2008) judicial docket with notation 'Cases 2007-3 and 2007-15 were found to be out of order.' The complaint was docketed in 2007 but never reached final determination on the merits.
2007-05: Appeal of Dr. George W. Mitchell vs. Evangel Presbytery. Case was withdrawn before adjudication and does not appear as a completed judicial decision in the SJC records.
2007-08: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Jones et al. against Louisiana Presbytery, finding that LAP erred in two ways: first, in failing to apply the correct constitutional standard for determining whether TE Wilkins had differences with the Westminster Standards (differences need not involve overt contradiction or denial, but can arise from different interpretations of wording or biblical exegesis); and second, in failing to adequately investigate and evaluate such differences as required by RAO 16-3(e)(5), thereby neglecting its duty to condemn erroneous opinions that injure the peace or purity of the church.
2007-09: The SJC sustained two consolidated complaints by TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery, annulling KEP's actions in empowering a Pulpit (Stated Supply Approval) Commission to act on behalf of the HKPC session without congregational consent, and annulling KEP's filing of a civil lawsuit in New Jersey state court to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The opinion extensively discusses the non-hierarchical nature of PCA polity and the limits of a presbytery's authority over local congregations.
2007-12: Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it read into its May 8, 2007 minutes the Shepherding Committee's report containing findings of sins and errors against TE Grady without due process, effectively imposing the censure of admonition without proper judicial procedure. The SJC sustained the complaint and directed the presbytery to expunge the Shepherding Committee report from its minutes.
2007-15: Complaint of TE Sang Chul Choi against Korean Central Presbytery. Case was found to be out of order on procedural grounds and was not substantively decided by the Standing Judicial Commission.
2007-16: The Standing Judicial Commission heard an appeal by TE John Grady from his conviction and censure by Southwest Florida Presbytery. The Commission sustained three of seven error specifications but found only one materially prejudicial. Critically, the Commission found that Presbytery misapplied BCO 13-9.c by claiming power to direct the minister to resign and then censuring him for refusal to comply; the Commission vacated the censure and remanded for reconsideration of appropriate punishment while the administrative suspension under BCO 31-10 remained in effect.
2008-04: Complaint of RE H. Lance Acree vs. Chesapeake Presbytery. Case was found to be out of order administratively and did not proceed to a substantive decision.
2008-05: Complaint of RE H. Lance Acree vs. Chesapeake Presbytery found to be out of order on procedural grounds.
2008-06: Complaint of Ruling Elder H. Lance Acree against Chesapeake Presbytery was found to be out of order on procedural grounds and did not proceed to a decision on the merits.
2008-07: Complaint of RE H. Lance Acree vs. Chesapeake Presbytery. Case found to be out of order and not completed by the SJC.
2008-08: Case 2008-08 (DE Joong Min Soh v. Philadelphia Presbytery) appears in the SJC docket list as found to be out of order. No substantive decision or opinion was issued.
2008-11: Chesapeake Presbytery appointed a commission to assume original jurisdiction over Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church of Relay, MD, without first making a finding that the Session had refused to act in a case of process. The SJC vacated the portion of the commission's mandate granting original jurisdiction under BCO 33-1, while upholding the portion related to receiving a reference from the Session.
2008-13: TE Meyerhoff complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in calling a special meeting to receive an initial report from the commission that had been appointed to assume original jurisdiction over Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church. In view of the judgment in Case 2008-11 vacating the commission's original jurisdiction mandate, the SJC found this complaint moot and directed Presbytery to note that in its minutes.
2008-14: TE Wes White complained that Siouxlands Presbytery erred when it refused to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into whether TE Greg Lawrence was teaching Federal Vision theology contrary to PCA doctrinal standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded the matter to Siouxlands Presbytery for a BCO 31-2 investigation, with a concurring opinion and a single dissenting opinion debating the proper standard of deference owed to the lower court.
2008-18: Complaint by TEs Hutchinson and Bulkeley against Western Carolina Presbytery's Inman Commission opinion regarding views of RE Payne expressed in a November 26, 2007 e-mail. The SJC found that Presbytery did not err because it would be inappropriate for the SJC to render judgment on the Biblical character of a man's views expressed in an e-mail without a more complete statement of those views and proper due process.
2009-02: Complaint of TE Morton H. Smith vs. Western Carolina Presbytery. The SJC sustained Smith's complaint in part, finding that Presbytery erred procedurally by immediately adopting a judgment against RE Payne's views without process. The SJC annulled the declaration made by Presbytery regarding RE Payne's views and remanded the case for proper adjudication.
2009-05: The Standing Judicial Commission affirmed that Presbytery of Western Carolina did not err in conducting its BCO 31-2 investigation of accusations against TE Craig Bulkeley or in finding no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC found no constitutional error in Presbytery's procedures and gave great deference to the lower court's discretionary judgment, noting that BCO 31-2 does not mandate specific procedures for investigations. The SJC also held that complainants Kirk Lyons and Robert Woodward lacked standing to bring complaints under BCO 43-1 and 11-4.
2009-07: Rocky Mountain Presbytery sustained a candidate's ordination exam who held the view that women could teach (but not preach or exercise authority) in church ministries under the authority of the church session. TE James Urish complained that Presbytery erred in sustaining the candidate's exam. The SJC affirmed Presbytery's decision, finding no clear error, as neither the Westminster Standards nor the BCO explicitly address this specific application of 1 Timothy 2:12.
2009-12: Southwest Florida Presbytery denied Paul Armes's complaint on the grounds that his excommunication removed his standing; the SJC unanimously remanded the case to the Presbytery after the Presbytery conceded error, holding that even an excommunicated person retains standing to complain against the censure itself.
2009-13: Complaint filed by Joseph Johnson against Southwest Florida Presbytery in 2009. The case was found to be administratively out of order by the Standing Judicial Commission at the 38th General Assembly (2010) and was not decided on the merits.
2009-14: The Ellisville Presbyterian Church Session filed a complaint against Grace Presbytery. The case was withdrawn before decision by the Standing Judicial Commission.
2009-16: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaints of TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery (cases 2007-09 and 2007-10). KEP erred when it empowered the Pulpit Commission to act on behalf of the church session without proper consent, and erred when it filed a civil action against TE Lee to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The decision affirms the non-hierarchical, voluntary nature of the PCA and its limited jurisdiction in civil matters.
2009-17: Michael McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery. Complaint found to be administratively out of order. No decision on merits.
2009-22: McNeil complained that Chesapeake Presbytery erred in denying his complaint against the Session's refusal to receive his charges against his wife after the Session had already censured him for abusive behavior; the SJC denied the complaint, applying a standard of great deference to the lower court and finding no clear procedural error.
2009-23: Illiana Presbytery appointed a Commission with broad powers to 'deal with matters' at Center Grove Presbyterian Church; the SJC found this was constitutional error because the language exceeded proper oversight bounds, but declared the error harmless since the Commission acted only as an investigating committee and the Session itself endorsed the Commission's findings.
2009-24: Complainant alleged that Pacific Presbytery erred in not opposing the ordination of Lee Irons as a Ruling Elder at New Life Burbank, given that Pacific Presbytery had previously denied Irons's application as a Teaching Elder candidate; the SJC denied the complaint, holding that each court retains discretion to evaluate candidates for ordination within its jurisdiction and that Presbytery's denial for Teaching Elder did not preclude a Session's ordination of the same man as Ruling Elder.
2009-25: Northern California Presbytery adopted an abstract resolution declaring six different views on the diaconate permissible for ministers and Sessions; the SJC sustained the complaints and annulled the resolution, holding that no court may issue binding abstract decrees beyond its proper jurisdictional exercise. A concurring opinion analyzed each of the six diaconal views in detail and set out standards (the GUMP/Kniseley framework) for when diaconal assistant practices are constitutionally permissible.
2009-27: Complaint of Dale Cutler against Platte Valley Presbytery. The case was found to be administratively out of order and not proceeded with on the merits.
2009-28: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to conduct an adequate BCO 31-2 investigation and to find a strong presumption of guilt against TE George Grant; the SJC sustained both complaints and remanded, finding the investigation record was incomplete and internally inconsistent, and that conduct described by the Presbytery's own Shepherding Committee as 'sin' required an explanation as to why no strong presumption of guilt existed.
2009-29: Michael McNeil v. Chesapeake Presbytery. Complaint found to be administratively out of order. No decision on merits.
2009-32: Case 2009-32 was a complaint filed by Russell Warren against Chesapeake Presbytery. The Standing Judicial Commission found the case to be administratively out of order and therefore did not issue a substantive decision on the merits.
2010-01: Mr. McNeil failed to appear at the hearing on Case 2010-01 and had not submitted a written brief. The Panel found the case abandoned and dismissed it.
2010-02: Case found to be administratively out of order by Standing Judicial Commission.
2010-03: The SJC ruled that McNeil's appeal was judicially out of order because he had not submitted to a regular trial, having refused to enter a plea or appear before Chesapeake Presbytery's Judicial Commission, and that his subsequent censure of suspension from the sacraments eliminated his standing to file further complaints against post-censure actions of the court.
2010-04: The SJC denied a complaint that Siouxlands Presbytery erred in finding no strong presumption of guilt in TE Joshua Moon after an investigation into allegations that his theological views on Federal Vision topics were heterodox, holding that deference to the presbytery was required absent clear error in the record. The case generated a concurring opinion offering procedural guidance on BCO 31-2 investigations versus BCO 32-2 charges, and a dissenting opinion by RE Haigler arguing the record showed unambiguous heterodoxy warranting a finding of strong presumption of guilt.
2010-05: The SJC found that Presbytery of Siouxlands erred in denying a complaint that sought the appointment of a committee to conduct a BCO 31-2 investigation into whether TE Greg Lawrence held or taught views associated with Federal Vision theology contrary to the PCA's doctrinal standards. The Court directed that the presbytery conduct the required investigation and established that credible reports affecting Christian character warrant investigation regardless of the evidentiary standards required for conviction.
2010-07: Case found to be Administratively Out of Order by the Standing Judicial Commission. No decision on merits was rendered.
2010-08: Case docketed for the 2011 General Assembly (39th GA). The case was found to be Judicially Out of Order and was not decided on the merits. This is a continuation of Michael McNeil's numerous complaints against Chesapeake Presbytery, appearing alongside similar cases 2010-09 through 2010-14, all of which were similarly ruled Judicially Out of Order.
2010-16: The SJC denied a complaint by Kirk Lyons challenging Western Carolina Presbytery's dismissal of charges he filed against TE Craig Bulkeley, finding no clear error in the presbytery's determination that grounds existed under BCO 31-8, 34-2, and 32-20 to decline the charges, though the SJC noted the presbytery erred (non-prejudicially) in denying Lyons standing, since filing BCO 32-2 charges brought him under the court's jurisdiction.
2010-17: TE David M. Sarafolean (Great Lakes Presbytery) requested the General Assembly / Standing Judicial Commission to cite Siouxlands Presbytery under BCO 40-4 and 40-5; the request was ruled administratively out of order.
2010-18: Gulfstream Presbytery was cited and appeared before the SJC regarding exceptions of substance found in its records; the SJC accepted the presbytery's response as acceptable, pending certification that the response was approved by the presbytery.
2010-24: The SJC found Case 2010-24 judicially out of order because Northwest Georgia Presbytery had rescinded the action complained against; a dissenting opinion argued that rescission does not automatically moot a complaint and that Mrs. Wood retained valid grounds related to Presbytery's failure to act.
2010-25: Case ruled administratively out of order. No decision issued on the merits.
2010-26: Korean Eastern Presbytery erred in dismissing TE Eliot Lee's charges against two Teaching Elders without conducting a trial; the SJC held that once properly drawn charges are filed, a Presbytery must proceed to adjudicate them unless it can demonstrate specific constitutional grounds for dismissal, and remanded the matter to KEP.
2010-27: The SJC found Mr. Ruff's complaint against Nashville Presbytery's failure to investigate a second Teaching Elder to be judicially out of order because the complaint was not filed within 30 days of the August 18, 2010 Presbytery meeting; a concurring objection argued this ruling was inherently unfair as Mr. Ruff was not notified of the meeting or that no action had been taken.
2010-28: Great Lakes Presbytery erred in approving Recommendation 5 of its Judicial Commission's report, which preemptively stated that Presbytery would not recommend or transfer TE Gonzales if he declined to demit or step away from ministry, because such action exceeded Presbytery's authority apart from censure after due judicial process.
2011-01: Mr. Choi's complaint was found Administratively Out of Order because it was prematurely filed with the General Assembly before Korean Central Presbytery had ruled on his complaint about the Presbytery's refusal to accept his charges.
2011-02: The SJC found that Great Lakes Presbytery erred in declaring TE Gonzales's second complaint out of order by conflating it with the first complaint (SJC 2010-28), but denied the complaint on the merits because TE Dupee's allegedly offending statement was made in his representative capacity as Committee Chairman, not personally, and therefore could not be the subject of a BCO 31-2 investigation.
2011-03: The SJC denied complaints that Covenant Presbytery's MNA Committee exceeded its authority in presenting a report and recommendations concerning the Mississippi Joint Committee on Campus Work, finding that the committee's investigation of the MJCCW structure was a natural extension of its assigned mandate to review campus minister salaries.
2011-05: Mr. Kim's complaint was found Administratively Out of Order because it was not filed with the Stated Clerk within 30 days following the last meeting of Korean Capital Presbytery on October 4, 2010.
2011-06: Complainants alleged Missouri Presbytery erred in failing to find a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held views contrary to the Westminster Standards in its BCO 31-2 investigation. The SJC found that MOP erred but declared the case moot because MOP had already conducted a trial of TE Meyers during the pendency of the case before the SJC.
2011-07: The 39th General Assembly had cited Warrior Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from 2007 and 2009. The SJC reviewed Warrior Presbytery's responses submitted under BCO 10-4 and found them acceptable, resolving the citation.
2011-08: Mr. Sherfey's complaint against James River Presbytery was ruled judicially out of order with defects that cannot be cured, because the bases of his complaint had not been adjudicated by JRP as required by BCO 43-2, and because the complaint to the General Assembly was not timely filed within the 30-day period of BCO 43-3. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.
2011-09: North Florida Presbytery was found to have erred in restoring deposed minister A. B. Scott to the office of Teaching Elder by a vote of 19-17, which the SJC determined did not satisfy the BCO 34-8 requirement that 'the general sentiment of the Church is strongly in his favor.' The SJC annulled NFP's actions and remanded the case; a lengthy dissent by RE Donahoe argued that BCO 34-8 does not require a super-majority and that the restoration vote is distinct from the evaluation of general sentiment.
2011-10: Mr. Testa's complaint against South Florida Presbytery was ruled administratively out of order because South Florida Presbytery had not yet acted on the matter. The SJC adopted the ruling 19 concurring, 1 not qualified, and 4 absent.
2011-11: Steven Hahn filed multiple complaints against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (PMWP) arising from his exclusion from worship at Christ the King Presbyterian Church pending a psychiatric evaluation, his subsequent conviction of three charges by PMWP, and PMWP's refusal to institute process against those he accused. The SJC denied all three complaints (2011-11, 2011-12, 2011-15), finding no clear error in PMWP's exercise of deference to the lower court, guilty verdict, or declination to appoint a prosecutor under BCO 31-8.
2011-13: Susan Elizabeth Spann filed an appeal alleging Oak Mountain Presbyterian Church committed excommunication without process and spiritual abuse, but the SJC dismissed the appeal as premature because there was no record of a judicial decision by OMPC nor any prior appeal to Evangel Presbytery as required by BCO 42-2. The SJC requested that Evangel Presbytery direct OMPC to provide a written response to Ms. Spann's concerns.
2011-14: RE Reese and TE Bech complained that Philadelphia Presbytery erred in declaring their complaint out of order after Presbytery refused to allow any questions of TE Jason Hsu regarding his views on women deacons when approving his transfer to City Line Church. The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that deeming parts of a complaint objectionable is insufficient grounds to rule the whole complaint out of order, though it agreed the proposed amends (removing TE Hsu) were not appropriate.
2011-17: TE William Smith complained against Mississippi Valley Presbytery's excommunication of TE Jeremy Smith who had confessed to adultery and abandoning his family. The SJC sustained one of the five allegations of error, finding that Presbytery incorrectly judged that the minister had 'refused' to appear since he was never formally cited, though the SJC did not annul the censure given other grounds for excommunication.
2011-18: Mr. Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed to comply with the SJC's prior ruling in Case 2009-28 when it concluded its BCO 31-2 investigation of TE George Grant via a case without process under BCO 38-1. The SJC found Presbytery had authority to use BCO 38-1 but erred in accepting a confession that was almost entirely abstract and did not adequately address particular sins against particular persons, and directed Presbytery to obtain an amended confession and sponsor reconciliation.
2011-19: Case was ruled administratively out of order. No detailed opinion or decision text was provided in the GA minutes.
2012-01: The SJC dismissed Case 2012-01 as judicially out of order on the ground that the action complained against was not in the Record of the Case. A dissenting opinion by three members argued the case should have been adjudicated, contending there was a complain able Session action in the record, as the SJC had itself indicated in the earlier related Case 2011-08; a written objection was also filed regarding TE Aquila's participation as panel chairman given his prior advice to the session at issue.
2012-02: TE Shawn Keating appealed his divestiture without censure by Warrior Presbytery, arguing Presbytery failed to follow BCO 34-10 procedures. The SJC sustained the appeal on procedural grounds, finding that Presbytery erred by proceeding to divestiture without first hearing the minister in his own defense, and voided the divestiture while noting Presbytery remained free to proceed again following proper procedures.
2012-03: TE Tarter appealed his deposition by Evangel Presbytery's Judicial Commission for failure to submit to presbytery authority. The SJC sustained multiple specifications of error — including that the Presbytery's committee had no authority to make certain demands, the indictment was inadequate, and hearsay evidence was improperly admitted — and remanded the case to Evangel Presbytery for constitutionally compliant process or dismissal.
2012-04: The SJC found TE Dwight Dunn's complaint against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery to be administratively out of order because the complaint was transmitted to a presbytery commission by the Stated Clerk rather than by motion and action of Presbytery, and because the commission's judgment was never brought back to Presbytery for approval as required by BCO 15-3.
2012-05: RE Gerald Hedman complained that Pacific Northwest Presbytery unconstitutionally adopted five not-guilty verdicts regarding TE Peter Leithart's teachings on baptism, covenants, imputation, justification, and union with Christ. The SJC denied the complaint, finding it was bound by the Record of the Case and that Complainant had not demonstrated clear error on the part of Presbytery, with concurring and dissenting opinions discussing the scope of review, standing, and concerns about Leithart's sacramental theology.
2012-06: The SJC ruled Case 2012-06 administratively out of order on two grounds: the complaint was not filed within the required 30-day period under BCO 43-2, and the complainant (a deacon who was not a commissioner to presbytery on the date of the action complained against) lacked standing under BCO 43-1.
2012-07: RE Mitchell appealed his indefinite suspension from office as Ruling Elder by the Presbytery of the Ascension, arising from allegations he broke a promise to take a sabbatical from Session and failed in his duties as Clerk of Session. The SJC vacated the judgment on Specification No. 2 (promise-breaking) and remanded for possible new trial, and reversed and dismissed Specification No. 6 (clerk duties) as insufficiently serious to warrant trial.
2012-08: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of TE Art Sartorius and six others against Presbytery of Siouxlands, finding that the Presbytery erred when it approved its Judicial Commission's verdict acquitting TE Gregory Lawrence of five charges related to Federal Vision theology and unconventional views on baptism and apostasy. The SJC identified serious procedural errors, specifically that the Judicial Commission admitted exculpatory post-indictment written statements from the defendant without subjecting them to cross-examination, contrary to BCO 35-5. The case was remanded to Presbytery for a new trial with detailed instructions regarding evidence procedures and Presbytery oversight.
2012-09: The SJC ruled Case 2012-09 administratively out of order because, although the complainant was a PCA member when he filed his original complaint to Presbytery on April 16, 2012, he had transferred to the OPC on April 28, 2012, and therefore lacked standing to bring his complaint to the SJC on August 16, 2012.
2012-10: The 40th General Assembly had cited Korean Capital Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from October 6, 2008. The SJC noted that Korean Capital Presbytery submitted responses approved by the Presbytery under BCO 10-4, and found those responses acceptable.
2013-01: TE Dunn and TE Pesnell complained that Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery erred in adopting its commission's recommendation to institute process and proceed to trial against TE David Swavely for alleged pastoral and spiritual abuse. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the Presbytery had sufficient authority to proceed to trial and that the errors alleged did not rise to a reversible level.
2013-02: Case 2013-02 (RE Warren Jackson vs. Northwest Georgia Presbytery) was found to be Administratively Out of Order by the Standing Judicial Commission. No substantive decision on the merits was reached.
2013-03: The SJC found Marshall's complaint judicially out of order on two grounds: that objections raised during a pending judicial case should be reserved for appeal rather than complaint (BCO 32-14; 42-3), and that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is pending (BCO 43-1). Three commissioners dissented, arguing BCO 32-14 did not apply before trial commenced and that BCO 43-1's exception is limited to pending appeals, not complaints filed before a trial occurs.
2013-04: The Session of Hope Community Church complained that Central Carolina Presbytery erred in adopting a policy requiring a multi-site session to eventually particularize its second worship site as a distinct new church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO expressly vests the Session with authority over the time and place of worship and the Presbytery's mandatory particularization requirement exceeded its constitutional powers and was annulled.
2013-06: The SJC sustained TE Gonzales's appeal, reversing and annulling Great Lakes Presbytery's divestiture of him without censure under BCO 34-10, because GLP failed to follow the required procedural steps: it did not record a finding that Gonzales had habitually failed to discharge his official functions, nor determine that his neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church, before proceeding to divestiture. The decision restored Gonzales to good standing in GLP while leaving open GLP's option to pursue proper process under BCO Chapter 31 or 34-10.
2013-07: The SJC sustained the Session of FPC North Port's complaint that Southwest Florida Presbytery erred when it remanded a previously out-of-order complaint back to the Session and when it directed and instructed the Session to initiate formal ecclesiastical process against a member without following the required steps of BCO 40-5. The Commission held that once the Original CM Complaint was found out of order, there was no matter for Presbytery to carry forward, and any subsequent instructions to the Session to initiate process were null and void.
2013-08: The SJC found the complaint administratively out of order because RE Jackson lacked standing as a non-commissioner to the January 2013 Presbytery meeting, but treated his correspondence as a credible BCO 40-5 report of an important delinquency by the Session of Midway Presbyterian Church, remitting the matter to Northwest Georgia Presbytery for constitutional disposition.
2013-09: Appeal by Mr. G. Rick Marshall vs. Pacific Presbytery. Case was withdrawn as prematurely filed and therefore did not proceed to a full SJC decision.
2013-10: The SJC sustained Rev. Latimer's appeal from his deposition for allegedly pursuing an unbiblical divorce, finding that Presbytery clearly erred because the record contained no conclusive evidence that his divorce filing — made on advice of counsel to protect his children — reflected an intent to divorce rather than a defensive legal measure; two concurring opinions addressed the Presbytery's choice of definite versus indefinite suspension.
2013-11: The SJC sustained the appeal of the Session of FPC North Port from the Presbytery of Southwest Florida's judgment suspending the Session, reversing the judgment in whole and dismissing all charges. The Commission held that Presbytery's citation and trial of the FPC Session for failure to initiate ecclesiastical process against a church member was constitutionally out of order, compounding the same errors identified in Case 2013-07, as Presbytery had failed to follow the required steps of BCO 40-5 before proceeding against the Session.
2013-12: The SJC dismissed the appeal and suspended the lower court's judgment indefinitely because Pacific Presbytery failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case — a defect that could not be remedied — and rebuked the Presbytery for failure to preserve and transmit trial testimony.
2014-01: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred in granting TE Hickey an exception to Larger Catechism 177 regarding admission of covenant children to the Lord's Supper. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint, remanding the case to the Presbytery because the record was insufficient to evaluate the minister's particular expression of his paedocommunion view.
2015-01: An inactive ruling elder's complaint to the Session was filed 78 days after the Session action complained against, exceeding the 60-day window of BCO 43-2. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order and voided all subsequent actions.
2015-02: An unsigned complaint was filed on TE Gearhart's behalf by a third party without standing, and TE Gearhart did not contact the PCA Clerk until 77 days after the Presbytery action (47 days past the BCO 43-3 deadline). The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed and the complainant did not give unqualified ratification.
2015-03: The SJC found Complaint 2015-03 moot because the issues it raised were adjudicated in the related Appeal 2015-08 (Hardie v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery).
